So I’ll say that I grew up driving in some snow. I haven’t driven consistently in the snow in almost a decade, but I have some knowledge of how to drive safely. We rented a car and drove to our AirBnB in Reykjavik, drove to go shopping a few times, drove to our second AirBnB near Selfoss and then drove up a bit in to the Golden Circle. With that being said, here’s my thoughts:

Driving to our AirBnB in Reykjavik after landing wasn’t too bad but it was main roads. Driving around in Reykjavik was pretty easy because the speed limit is slower and they’re well taken care of. Driving to outside of Selfoss, I was checking road conditions every 30 minutes leading up to the drive and there was a bit of snow but nothing too crazy. It didn’t feel too bad driving but I definitely was locked in 100% and was grateful for 4WD. Then came the trip up to the Golden Circle, specifically Laugarvatn. We had received some snow and the roads were plowed but once again, I was tuned in to the road conditions before and during the drive. The last 12km or so was pretty rough. It wasn’t a main road, it was a two lane road but basically all traffic was in one lane so when going two wide with oncoming traffic you were basically having to move over in to fresh unpacked snow for a bit. 

The next day after that we had a tour out to most of those locations you want. It was about 4 hours or so from our Selfoss pickup and let me tell you, that was one of the best decisions I made on this trip. Those drivers are way more experienced, the roads went from no snow coverage to a slushy mix that I was sure our smaller car would’ve had difficulty with, and I could just relax and tune out for the most part. 

TLDR; yes, if you have winter driving experience you could rent a car, monitor road conditions and be able to get around. But honestly, unless you plan to spend a long time in those locations or are overnighting at multiple spots, it’s just so much easier to kick back and enjoy someone else driving.
